reporting.lead_count_basis: Open opportunities across all three pipelines: 181 in (1) PROJECT: Lead Qualification, 27 in (2) PROJECT: Sales Pipeline, 51 in STORE: Material Pipeline.

exclusions._comment: Reconciles the netted metrics back to raw. Excluded records are not dropped; they stay in conversations[] / new_leads[] carrying the flag that excluded them.
exclusions.unanswered_note: The (416) 433-9872 inbound call carries call status 'voicemail', so it is a real lead and is counted, not netted out as a no-voicemail miss.
exclusions.drift_excluded_note: 12 contacts hold call-queue with no lead: tag and would each be an untagged_in_queue finding; all sit in 0a. New Lead, which drift_excluded_stages suppresses. The untagged_in_queue metric still reports the live queue depth. Separately, 49 open STORE: Material Pipeline opportunities carry no lead: tag and are not treated as categorization_miss — that pipeline is retail material and was never part of the lead-qualification workflow.

leads_by_tag._comment: Contact tags across the 259 currently-open opportunities, not lifetime tag history. Lifetime totals for reference: lead: hot 108, lead: warm 177, lead: cold 168, lead: unqualified 158, lead: lost 7, lead: rate-shopper 0, stale_lead 774.

avg_days_in_stage._comment: 0b. Far Out (Cold) is skewed by the 93-record bulk-timestamp cohort; excluding it the stage average is roughly 118 days.

opportunity_status_counts._comment: Lifetime totals across all three pipelines. Abandoned is by far the largest bucket, as expected.

reporting.store_pipeline_note: STORE: Material Pipeline holds 51 open opportunities, 28 of them in '3. + 8d - Final Follow-up (Auto)'. Retail material sales, distinct from project work, running its own +3d/+8d cadence. No stale thresholds are defined for this pipeline, so no staleness prediction is made for it. Note 13 open records still sit in stage '6a. Closed - Won' while their status is not won — a stage/status divergence worth cleaning up.

stale_thresholds_used._comment: Echoed from platform-settings/ghl-workflow.json so a threshold change shows up in the diff.

meeting_window_summary._comment: The window any new Meeting-scheduled follow-up sequence must fit inside. The 30-day threshold counts from stage entry, so appointments booked far out shrink the usable runway.
meeting_window_summary.note: 22 of 24 appointments were matched by pulling calendar events for user rAMFCiXbAjJOEjtyyvmn over Apr 1 - Aug 31 and joining on contactId; this is a better match rate than the 3/21 and 10/41 of earlier runs. The two unmatched are John Ap Disposal (no appointment found) and Tina Tran (appointment predates the pull window).

data_quality_notes: 93 of 119 open 0b. Far Out (Cold) opportunities share one identical lastStageChangeAt (~Oct 29 2025), consistent with a bulk stage migration. Their day counts are not real per-lead staleness and are reported as one aggregate finding rather than 93 rows.

An undocumented tag 'abandoned-stale' appears on 7 open opportunities (Bash Saqr, Karan Thakar, Tina Tran among them) where the workflow documents 'stale_lead'. Reported as-is, never folded into stale_lead.

opportunities_search-opportunity has no updated-at sort or filter, so stage moves and closes in the window were found by pulling every open record in each thresholded stage plus all 302 Project Won records and filtering on lastStageChangeAt / lastStatusChangeAt. Store pipeline was pulled in full (66 records).

Stage populations use status=open. Querying status=all returns every record whose last stage was that one before it closed (e.g. 921 vs 15 for 0a. New Lead), which would overstate live volume roughly 60x.
